approvedDeviation: #821 Wave 2: people_profile.cadence_days relaxes its CHECK from (cadence_days > 0) to (cadence_days >= 0) so 0 means "never — cadence disabled" and a person the owner never wants nagged about is finally storable; the add_person and set_cadence input schemas drop their `minimum` to 0 to match, and negatives stay refused at both layers. No new table and no new column: the widened domain rides the already-walked people_profile column, and an export must carry it verbatim or a restore would coerce a silenced person back into the overdue queue. It does add rung two to VAULT_MIGRATIONS — a vault-preserving people_profile rebuild (create/copy/drop/rename, then re-create the purge index and the updated_at trigger) that carries the relaxed CHECK to vaults already stamped user_version 1, since editing the baseline text alone reaches only newly created files; the rebuild re-creates the same columns in the same order, so the export walk sees an unchanged table shape. The same change set gives share_party_vault_binding a vault-side writer for the LINK CEREMONY — which previously had none, so "is this person linked" lived as gateway-side JSON and now upserts through share/party-vault-binding.ts. That table is already registered in schema/tables.ts as share.party_vault_binding, so the canonical walk carries the new rows unchanged. Export completeness re-audited in packages/vault/src/gateway/portable-export.ts. No adapter, no content bytes, no table dropped.
